ut_bridger_jack_butte.blurb: Bridger Jack Butte is a big sandstone butte in the Indian Creek climbing zone of San Juan County, Utah, standing apart from the neighbouring Bridger Jack towers. It is a trad objective with a mix of multi-pitch and single-pitch lines on broad faces, and the 11 climbs here run from 5.10 into the 5.12 range, with most of them around 5.11. Most routes face east, with a few on the west side. This is a place for confident crack and face leaders rather than beginners. Spring and fall are the comfortable seasons in this semi-arid country.

ut_bridge_area.blurb: A small cluster of bolted lines beside the road in Maple Canyon, central Utah, on the left as you drive up, either side of the road bridge. The 11 sport routes are mostly 5.11, with a handful of 5.10s and a single 5.9, so it suits climbers who are past the beginner stage and want steady, sustained pitches. The walls mostly face north and hold shade through much of the day, which makes it a reasonable pick when the sun is strong. It is an easy stop to pair with other roadside walls up the canyon.

ut_lewis_carroll_wall.blurb: Lewis Carroll Wall is a short basalt wall in Pine Valley, northwest of St. George in southwest Utah, sitting along the trail just beyond the Playpen. It holds 11 routes, mostly sport with a few trad lines, and every one falls in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, so it is a good fit for climbers working through the low-to-mid grades of hard. Pine Valley basalt is technical face climbing with plenty of friction, and routes run up to about 100 feet. In winter the sun arrives in the morning and can turn the wall hot; in summer it goes into shade from mid-afternoon.

ut_northside_routes.blurb: Northside Routes is a small sandstone area north of the Colorado River near Moab, reached from the River Road corridor. All 11 climbs are trad, and many are multi-pitch. They cover a broad spread, from a single 5.8 and a group of 5.9s through 5.10, with a couple of harder lines at 5.11 and 5.12. That makes it one of the friendlier trad stops along River Road for moderate leaders. Moab sandstone is fragile when wet, so wait out rain before climbing.

ut_ragnarock.blurb: Ragnarock is a boulder zone above the main wash in the Swett Hills, a short drive from Cedar City in southwest Utah. It has 11 problems that tend toward steeper, harder climbing than the lower wash, spanning an easy warm-up to V7, with the bulk sitting between V4 and V5. Rock quality is described as good, with friction that can be hard on skin if you stay long. The trail up from the main trailhead has grown faint over the years, so it can take some route-finding to reach.
